fields.name: Albuskjell
fields.statusText: The field is under development, and the production is planned to start in 2028.

fields.name: Alve
fields.statusText: Production from Alve is constrained by the commercial agreement with the Norne licence and the gas handling capacity on the Norne FPSO. Excess capacity on the FPSO in recent years has made it possible to process larger volumes of gas from Alve. The long-term activity on the field is to optimise production. Andvare is drilled and produced from a well slot available on Norne.

fields.name: Alve Nord
fields.statusText: The production started in August 2026.

fields.name: Alvheim
fields.statusText: Due to greater in-place volumes and longer infill wells, Alvheim has had a significant increase in the estimated recoverable volumes of oil and gas since the PDO. Other accumulations, such as Kobra East and Gekko which were put into production in 2023, have also contributed to increased production.

fields.name: Atla
fields.statusText: Atla was shut down in 2023, and decommissioning is ongoing.

fields.name: Balder
fields.statusText: Balder and Ringhorne are in the tail production phase but still have significant remaining production potential. The objective of extended field life and the relocation of the Jotun FPSO is to utilise the existing infrastructure in the area to increase the field recovery and develop the nearby discoveries.

fields.name: Bauge
fields.statusText: The production is lower than anticipated, partly due to lower reservoir quality and downtime of the process facility. Identifying and maturation of infill targets is ongoing.

fields.name: Berling
fields.statusText: The field is under development, and the production is planned to start in 2028.

fields.name: Bestla
fields.statusText: The field is under development, and the production is planned to start in 2027.

fields.name: Blane
fields.statusText: Production from the field has generally been good, but the water cut is increasing. The production is restricted by sufficient gas from Ula available for gas lift, by oil-in-water limits and other technical problems.

fields.name: Brage
fields.statusText: Brage has been producing for a long time, and work is still ongoing to find new ways to increase recovery from the field. New wells are being drilled, often combined with exploration of near field prospects.

fields.name: Breidablikk
fields.statusText: The production has been higher than anticipated. Drilling of new wells is ongoing.

fields.name: Brynhild
fields.statusText: Brynhild was shut down in 2018, and the subsea template was removed in 2021.

fields.name: Byrding
fields.statusText: Production has resumed after being shut down since December 2022 due to technical issues in the well.

fields.name: Bøyla
fields.statusText: The recoverable volume estimates are significantly higher than in the original Bøyla PDO, partly because of the production from Frosk.

fields.name: Cod
fields.statusText: Cod was shut down in 1998. The facility was removed in 2013, and the production licence area was relinquished in 2022.

fields.name: Draugen
fields.statusText: The field lifetime has been prolonged, and the production licence that includes the Draugen field has been extended to 2040. Several initiatives have been launched to enable future profitable production from the Draugen field, such as power from shore, near-field exploration, increased water injection, and new infill wells.

fields.name: Duva
fields.statusText: The production has been higher than anticipated, due to additional processing capacity available at the Gjøa platform and better performance of the oil production wells. The oil production is on decline, and start of the gas blowdown phase will depend on the performance of the oil producers.

fields.name: Dvalin
fields.statusText: The production from Dvalin is stable on plateau.

fields.name: Edda
fields.statusText: Edda was shut down in 1998, and the facility was removed in 2012.

fields.name: Edvard Grieg
fields.statusText: Edvard Grieg production has come off plateau. The field has been producing better than expected and the recoverable volumes have increased significantly since the PDO due to excellent reservoir performance. Several additional wells have been drilled and are planned going forward. Test production from the Troldhaugen discovery started in 2021 and continues.

fields.name: Eirin
fields.statusText: The production started in May 2026.

fields.name: Ekofisk
fields.statusText: The production from Ekofisk is maintained at a high level through continuous water injection, drilling of production and injection wells, and well interventions. Water injection is extended in the southern part of the field. Key challenges are identifying the remaining oil pockets in a mature, waterflooded reservoir, as well as handling the increasing volumes of produced water. Infill drilling on Ekofisk is expected to continue throughout the lifetime of the field. Various drilling methods are being studied to reduce drilling costs, for example coiled tubing drilling.

fields.name: Eldfisk
fields.statusText: Drilling of additional wells on Eldfisk is continuing. Drilling targets are also being matured in the eastern structure, Eldfisk East. Production from Eldfisk North started in 2024, and further development of the structure is ongoing. Coiled tubing drilling (CTD) is being considered for injection wells on Eldfisk S, after the technical success of CTD executed on Ekofisk injectors.

fields.name: Embla
fields.statusText: As part of the Eldfisk II development project, Embla was tied to the Eldfisk S facility, extending the lifetime for Embla. Because of the complexity of the reservoir, there are no plans other than optimising the existing production wells. Currently, there are four active producers.

fields.name: Enoch
fields.statusText: The field is in its late tail phase. The production from Enoch is dependent on the lifetime of the Brae facility.

fields.name: Fenja
fields.statusText: The production has been lower than planned due to the field’s overall lower potential, increasing water cut and a rising gas-oil ratio. The discovery 6406/11-1 S (Vidsyn) was drilled in 2025. Work is ongoing to evaluate further appraisal of prospects in the vicinity and to establish a development project.

fields.name: Fenris
fields.statusText: The field is under development. The development of Fenris is coordinated with the further development of the Valhall field. The production is planned to start in 2027.

fields.name: Flyndre
fields.statusText: Flyndre was shut down in 2023.

fields.name: Fram
fields.statusText: An extra gas module dedicated to Fram on the Troll C platform started operation in 2020. Production from the Fram area is optimised within the available capacities at Troll C. Active exploration is ongoing in the area.

fields.name: Fram H-Nord
fields.statusText: Fram H-Nord well is currently shut and has not been producing during the year 2025 due to technical issues in the well.

fields.name: Frigg
fields.statusText: Frigg was shut down in 2004, and final disposal of the facilities was completed in 2010. An appraisal well was drilled on Frigg in 2019. The development of the Yggdrasil area may provide an opportunity for a redevelopment of the field.

fields.name: Frøy
fields.statusText: Frøy was shut down in 2001, and the facility was removed in 2002. The ongoing development of the Hugin field includes a redevelopment of Frøy with a normally unmanned platform, Hugin B, tied-back to Hugin A.

fields.name: Gaupe
fields.statusText: Gaupe was shut down in 2018. Decommissioning of the subsea facilities must be completed by the end of 2028.

fields.name: Gimle
fields.statusText: Gimle was temporarily shut down due to low reservoir pressure. A new production well was drilled in the area between the Gimle and Sindre fields, and there has been test production from the well in 2025.

fields.name: Gina Krog
fields.statusText: Gina Krog is producing at gas plateau; oil production, however, is declining. To keep the gas production at plateau, all gas injectors have been converted into production wells. The use of gas lift is being evaluated for some of the wells. In 2024, a new oil pipeline to Sleipner A was installed, and the FSO was removed from the field. Modification work is ongoing on the platform to prepare for low pressure production as well as the tie-in of the subsea template on the Eirin field.

fields.name: Gjøa
fields.statusText: Production from Gjøa has started to decline. Work is focusing on production optimisation and maturation of new production opportunities, such as natural gas lift, infill drilling and near-field exploration targets. Work is ongoing to develop Gjøa to become an area hub.

fields.name: Glitne
fields.statusText: Glitne was shut down in 2013, and decommissioning was completed in 2015.

fields.name: Goliat
fields.statusText: Production regularity has been below expectation since production start-up. Continuous maintenance and modification work along with several revision stops have resulted in a gradually improved regularity of the facility. A solution for Goliat gas export is being considered, which will contribute to extend the lifetime of the field. Several infill wells have been drilled since start up. More infill and exploration wells are planned in the coming years.

fields.name: Grane
fields.statusText: The recoverable volumes have increased since the initial PDO estimates. A permanent reservoir monitoring system installed on the seabed provides more detailed seismic data for improved reservoir management. Several wells have been drilled, and new wells are being planned, most of them as multilateral wells.

fields.name: Gudrun
fields.statusText: The production is off plateau and on decline. Gudrun has been supplied with power from shore through the area solution for the Utsira High since 2024. The Gudrun installation has flexibility for tie-in of discoveries in the area.

fields.name: Gullfaks
fields.statusText: Drilling of new wells on Gullfaks has been challenging for many years due to overpressured areas in the Shetland/Lista interval. Production from the Shetland/Lista reservoirs has gradually contributed to reduced overpressures and improved drillability. Additional wells are being drilled continuously from all platforms and well interventions are of vital importance to maintain production levels.

fields.name: Gullfaks Sør
fields.statusText: The Gullfaks Sør production is on decline, but the field still has significant remaining gas volumes. New wells are continuously drilled in the area with a licence-owned rig. Work is ongoing to optimise gas injection on the field and timing of blowdown of the gas cap in Gullfaks Sør Statfjord.

fields.name: Gungne
fields.statusText: Gungne is in its late tail production phase. Only one well is currently on production, and there is no production from the well on the Gamma High structure.

fields.name: Gyda
fields.statusText: Gyda was shut down in 2020, and the facility was removed in 2022.

fields.name: Halten Øst
fields.statusText: Halten Øst will be developed in two phases. Production from the first phase started in March 2025, and the next phase is scheduled to start production in 2029.

fields.name: Hanz
fields.statusText: Production has been lower than expected due to low reservoir pressure and limited pressure support from the injection well. Consequently, recoverable volume estimates have been reduced.

fields.name: Heidrun
fields.statusText: The production from Heidrun is maintained through water and gas injection as well as drilling of new production and injection wells. Different methods are being evaluated and implemented to enhance oil and gas recovery and prolong the lifetime of the field.

fields.name: Heimdal
fields.statusText: The production from Heimdal ceased in 2020. Heimdal was used as a gas processing centre until mid-2023. Decommissioning of the facilities must be completed by the end of 2028.

fields.name: Hod
fields.statusText: The production from Hod B started in 2022. The original Hod platform awaits decommissioning within 2026.

fields.name: Huldra
fields.statusText: Huldra was shut down in 2014, and the facility was removed in 2019.

fields.name: Hyme
fields.statusText: The production is lower than anticipated, mainly due to downtime associated with the Njord process facility. The current production strategy for Hyme is to optimise the drainage by balancing water injection versus development of pressure and water cut in the production well.

fields.name: Idun Nord
fields.statusText: The production started in August 2026.

fields.name: Irpa
fields.statusText: The field is under development. The production is planned to start in 2026.

fields.name: Islay
fields.statusText: The well is producing cyclically at a low rate.

fields.name: Ivar Aasen
fields.statusText: Since start-up of production, additional injection and production wells have been drilled. Ivar Aasen production is on decline. The Symra field is under development as a tie-back to Ivar Aasen, and production is expected to start in 2026. The Ivar Aasen platform is equipped for tie-in of other nearby discoveries.

fields.name: Jette
fields.statusText: Jette was shut down in 2016, and the subsea template was removed in 2019.

fields.name: Johan Castberg
fields.statusText: The production started in March 2025.

fields.name: Johan Sverdrup
fields.statusText: Johan Sverdrup accounts for about one third of the Norwegian oil production. The field is currently producing with high regularity at plateau, close to the current oil handling capacity. The oil handling capacity was increased after a capacity test in 2023. A third development phase is currently being prepared.

fields.name: Jotun
fields.statusText: Jotun was shut down in 2016, and Jotun B was removed in 2020. The Jotun FPSO is upgraded and relocated to the Balder and Ringhorne Øst fields to continue operation.

fields.name: Knarr
fields.statusText: Knarr was shut down in 2022 and the FPSO was removed from the field. Decommissioning of the subsea facilities must be completed by 2028.

fields.name: Kristin
fields.statusText: Kristin production is in the tail phase. Future plans to increase recovery from the field include measures to extend the lifetime of existing wells through well interventions, as well as opportunities for additional wells. The development of Kristin South is being carried out in several phases. Phase 1 is in production and further development considered as the next phase.

fields.name: Kvitebjørn
fields.statusText: The production on Kvitebjørn is declining. New producers are being drilled, and further drilling is planned.

fields.name: Lille-Frigg
fields.statusText: Lille-Frigg was shut down in 1999, and the installation was removed in 2001. The ongoing development of the Fulla field includes a redevelopment of Lille-Frigg as a subsea tie-back to the production platform on the Hugin field.

fields.name: Maria
fields.statusText: Production from Maria Phase 2 has started and is contributing to increased recovery from the central part of the Garn Formation, which was previously not drained by existing wells. In addition, two potential infill targets have been identified and matured, with planned drilling in 2027–2028.

fields.name: Martin Linge
fields.statusText: To maintain production on the field, continuous well-intervention campaigns and drilling of new wells are planned.

fields.name: Marulk
fields.statusText: The production from Marulk is in the decline phase. It is limited by the commercial agreement with Norne and the gas handling capacity on the Norne FPSO. Marulk utilises excess capacity when available on the FPSO.

fields.name: Mikkel
fields.statusText: The production from Mikkel is governed by the reserved capacity on Åsgard B. No new wells have been drilled since 2020, and the field currently produces from four wells. A project for late life production is in its initial phase.

fields.name: Mime
fields.statusText: Mime was shut down in 1993, and the facility was removed in 1999.

fields.name: Morvin
fields.statusText: Drilling of new wells on Morvin is technically and economically challenging. The focus is therefore to ensure continued production from the existing wells, for example by conducting well interventions.

fields.name: Murchison
fields.statusText: Murchison was shut down in 2014, and the platform was removed in 2017.

fields.name: Njord
fields.statusText: In 2024, production from Njord has been lower than anticipated, due to delayed wells and downtime of the process plant. Njord is planned to receive power from shore via the Draugen platform in a few years and thus be partially electrified.

fields.name: Nordøst Frigg
fields.statusText: Nordøst Frigg was shut down in 1993, and the facility was removed in 1996. The development of the Yggdrasil area may provide an opportunity for a redevelopment of the field.

fields.name: Norne
fields.statusText: The production from Norne is in the decline phase. Production challenges are related to reservoir souring, increasing water cut, scale and well integrity due to aging facilities. The key activities include identifying new well targets and optimising the water injection strategy.

fields.name: Nova
fields.statusText: The production from Nova is in accordance with the reserved capacity at the Gjøa processing facility. The main focus is to optimise pressure support to the production wells.

fields.name: Oda
fields.statusText: Oda is in the tail end of the production lifetime. Drilling of the production wells has shown that the reservoir is more complex and smaller than anticipated. Consequently, the estimated recoverable volumes have been decreased. There are no plans for further development of the field.

fields.name: Odin
fields.statusText: Odin was shut down in 1994, and the facility was removed in 1997. The development of the Yggdrasil area may provide an opportunity for a redevelopment of the field.

fields.name: Ormen Lange
fields.statusText: The production from Ormen Lange is declining, and increased recovery is a key focus. The subsea compression system was installed and started up in 2025 to extend the field’s lifetime and increase recovery.

fields.name: Oseberg
fields.statusText: The strategy for the main Oseberg reservoirs is to balance oil production with increasing gas offtake. To increase oil recovery from the northern part of the field, the inlet pressure on the Oseberg C facility has been reduced. New production wells are continuously being drilled to enhance oil recovery. The first dedicated gas production wells were drilled in 2023.

fields.name: Oseberg Sør
fields.statusText: Further maturation of drilling targets is a focus area, but lack of available well slots is a challenge. Several projects are under evaluation to increase recovery from Oseberg Sør.

fields.name: Oseberg Øst
fields.statusText: Oseberg Øst is at the tail end of its production phase and the main challenge is to maximise the oil recovery within the field lifetime. To increase production, the focus is on drainage strategy, including optimisation of injection and well interventions. Maximising the gas production rate is also of importance, as the produced gas is used as fuel supply for the platform power generator. A decommissioning plan for the Oseberg Øst field was submitted to the authorities in 2024.

fields.name: Oselvar
fields.statusText: Oselvar was shut down in 2018, and the facility was removed in 2022.

fields.name: Rev
fields.statusText: The estimated volumes have been reduced since the PDO. The field has been producing with very short production periods and long pressure build-up periods since 2013.

fields.name: Ringhorne Øst
fields.statusText: The field is in its tail production phase, but there is still development potential. The amended PDO for Balder and Ringhorne, approved in 2020, extends the field’s lifetime and increases the production as a result of increased capacity in the area. A new infill well was drilled on Ringhorne Øst in 2025.

fields.name: Sigyn
fields.statusText: The field is in its late tail production phase. An infill well was put on production on Sigyn East in 2022, and the existing producer was converted to a gas injector. There has only been production from Sigyn East after the well on Sigyn West ceased producing in early 2024. A new infill well is planned to be drilled on Sigyn West in 2026. The well shall produce from both the Triassic and Jurassic reservoirs.

fields.name: Sindre
fields.statusText: Sindre has been shut down for a long time due to low reservoir pressure. Cyclic production is planned in the future. A new production well was drilled in the area between the Sindre and Gimle fields in 2024, and there has been test productionfrom the well in 2025.

fields.name: Skarv
fields.statusText: The oil production from Skarv is declining, and gas injection is important for oil recovery. Gas blowdown has started in 2022 from parts of the reservoir and will continuously be evaluated. Work is ongoing to evaluate the potential of infill wells and prospects in the area.

fields.name: Skirne
fields.statusText: Skirne was shut down in 2023, and decommissioning is ongoing.

fields.name: Skogul
fields.statusText: The recoverable volume estimates for Skogul are higher than in the PDO. The production has been higher than anticipated, even though the oil production is steadily declining due to increasing water cut.

fields.name: Skuld
fields.statusText: Skuld is in the tail end production phase. Identification of new infill drilling targets and prevention of scale problems are the main focus areas for Skuld.

fields.name: Sleipner Vest
fields.statusText: Sleipner Vest is in the middle of the tail production phase. To increase the production from the field, the inlet pressure at Sleipner T has been reduced and is planned to be reduced further in the coming years. A drilling campaign started in 2025 and will continue in 2026.

fields.name: Sleipner Øst
fields.statusText: Sleipner Øst is in the late tail production phase. The main focus is on increasing reserves and decreasing production decline. It is expected that Sleipner Øst continues operation for tied-back fields after cease of own production. Sleipner has been partly supplied with power from shore via the Gina Krog platform since 2024.

fields.name: Snorre
fields.statusText: Several measures to increase oil recovery from Snorre are being considered. Possible third-party tie-ins may lead to further development of the field.

fields.name: Snøhvit
fields.statusText: The production from Snøhvit is in the plateau phase. Since production started, additional production wells have been drilled in different structures. Work is ongoing to prepare for onshore compression and electrification in order to significantly reduce CO2 emissions from the onshore facility at Melkøya.

fields.name: Solveig
fields.statusText: Solveig Phase 2, which includes installation of two new subsea templates, is under development.

fields.name: Statfjord
fields.statusText: Work is ongoing to extend the lifetime of the field. Plans include prolonging the lifetime of the platforms and drilling of many new wells in the years to come. Satellite fields tied-back to Statfjord as well as nearby discoveries will benefit from the lifetime extension.

fields.name: Statfjord Nord
fields.statusText: The lifetime extension of the Statfjord C facility opens for additional wells for the field. A drilling campaign is planned for 2026.

fields.name: Statfjord Øst
fields.statusText: The field is affected by pressure depletion due to depressurisation of the Statfjord field. The lifetime extension of the Statfjord C facility opens for additional opportunities for the field. The focus going forward is on optimizing the wells and handling challenges related to sand production. A drilling campaign towards the end of 2026 is being considered.

fields.name: Svalin
fields.statusText: The production has been lower than anticipated in the PDO and is declining due to increasing water cut. Plans for further development of the field include possible infill wells and exploration activities.

fields.name: Sygna
fields.statusText: The production from Sygna is stable, and the strategy is to keep the reservoir pressure constant by water injection.

fields.name: Symra
fields.statusText: The production started in April 2026.

fields.name: Tambar
fields.statusText: Tambar is currently in the late life phase. The production is declining due to decreased reservoir pressure and increasing water cut. Production from Tambar is dependent on the lifetime of the Ula field which is planned to be shut down in 2028.

fields.name: Tambar Øst
fields.statusText: The production from Tambar Øst had been shut-in temporarily since 2019 for pressure build-up, and was restarted in 2023. Production from Tambar Øst is dependent on the lifetime of the Ula field which is planned to be shut down in 2028.

fields.name: Tommeliten A
fields.statusText: Tommeliten A has maintained stable production since start-up. All planned wells have been drilled, with seven currently producing and four awaiting final work before start-up. Production in 2025 has exceeded previous estimates, even though not all wells are in operation.

fields.name: Tommeliten Gamma
fields.statusText: The field is under development, and the production is planned to start in 2029.

fields.name: Tor
fields.statusText: Several of the wells have experienced higher water cut than anticipated. The original facility was removed in 2024.

fields.name: Tordis
fields.statusText: Tordis is in tail production phase and the production is maintained through pressure support and well interventions. New well targets are being matured. There are no unused slots, and new wells must therefore be drilled as sidetracks from existing wells.

fields.name: Trestakk
fields.statusText: The production from the field has been lower than anticipated due to poorer reservoir properties than predicted and lower gas injection volumes. Starting in mid-2023, an updated gas injection strategy has been implemented, resulting in stabilised production rates. New infill targets are being evaluated.

fields.name: Troll
fields.statusText: More than two million reservoir metres have been drilled on Troll. Drilling of new oil production wells on Troll concluded altogether; however, the need for future oil wells will be considered regularly. Various measures have been implemented and are in the preparation phase to improve gas capacity and production, such as drilling of several new gas wells in the coming years. A new gas export solution from Troll B to the Kvitebjørn gas pipeline started operation in 2025.

fields.name: Troll Brent B
fields.statusText: During drilling of the production well, oil reserves were proven to be significantly lower than originally assumed. It was therefore decided to be uneconomical to start production on the Troll Brent B field. The well was plugged; however, the well slot is available to be used for potential new targets on Troll Vest.

fields.name: Trym
fields.statusText: Trym production started up again in 2024, after a major redevelopment project on the Tyra field in the Danish sector.

fields.name: Tune
fields.statusText: The Tune field is in its tail production phase and produces cyclically. The main challenges for Tune are old infrastructure and low reservoir pressure. The field was shut-down since 2022 because of well integrity issues. The production started again in 2024.

fields.name: Tyrihans
fields.statusText: Drilling of new wells is challenging on Tyrihans because of reservoir depletion. To increase recovery for both oil and gas, work related to low pressure production and possibilities for infill wells is ongoing.

fields.name: Tyrving
fields.statusText: The field has produced higher than expected, mainly due to delayed water cut.

fields.name: Ula
fields.statusText: Production from Ula is in the late life phase. Gas supply for WAG is challenging and the production is declining. It is planned to cease production in 2028. The resource estimates on Ula are more than three times higher than the original PDO estimates.

fields.name: Urd
fields.statusText: Challenges for Urd are poor pressure support, increasing water cut, problems with the well stream (slugging and sand production) and failure of subsea/well equipment. A sidetrack of an existing producer was drilled in 2023.

fields.name: Utgard
fields.statusText: Utgard is currently producing from two wells, and the key challenge on the field is the high water production. A sidetrack well in the eastern segment came on stream in 2025.

fields.name: Vale
fields.statusText: Vale was shut down in 2023. Decommissioning of the subsea template must be completed by the end of 2028.

fields.name: Valemon
fields.statusText: Due to production experience and rapid pressure decline in the reservoirs, the estimated recoverable volumes have been significantly reduced since the PDO. The second drilling campaign including four new production wells started in 2021, and the last of the wells came on stream in mid-2023. The production contribution from the new wells is below expectations. After closing of the Heimdal facility in 2023, permanent rerouting of the Valemon gas export via Kvitebjørn to the Kollsnes terminal was initiated.

fields.name: Valhall
fields.statusText: The Valhall field has produced more than one billion barrels of oil equivalents, which is three times more than the original PDO estimate. New completion technology to increase recovery from the tight chalk reservoir is implemented in a new producer drilled on the northern flank of Valhall. Drilling of new wells will continue in the foreseeable future. Decommissioning of the QP, PCP and DP facilities must be completed by the end of 2026. Start-up of production from the new platform (PWP) is planned for 2027.

fields.name: Varg
fields.statusText: The decommissioning plan for Varg was approved in 2001. The plan then was to produce until summer 2002, but measures implemented on the field prolonged its lifetime. A new decommissioning plan was submitted in 2015. Varg was shut down in 2016, and the facility was removed in 2018.

fields.name: Vega
fields.statusText: Vega production is on decline. The main reservoir management focus on Vega is to secure stable production from all the three structures within the available gas capacity on Gjøa. The strategy is to prioritise production from Vega Sør and then fill up the capacity with production from Vega Nord and Sentral.

fields.name: Verdande
fields.statusText: The production started in December 2025.

fields.name: Veslefrikk
fields.statusText: Veslefrikk was shut down in 2022, and Veslefrikk B was removed from the field. Decommissioning must be completed by the end of 2027.

fields.name: Vest Ekofisk
fields.statusText: The field is under development, and the production is planned to start in 2028.

fields.name: Vigdis
fields.statusText: The strategy on Vigdis is to maintain reservoir pressure by water injection, while maximising production capacity and regularity. New well targets are being matured. There are no unused slots, and new wells must therefore be drilled as sidetracks from existing wells.

fields.name: Vilje
fields.statusText: The recoverable volume estimates are significantly higher than in the original PDO, but the field is on decline with a high water cut. There is currently only one oil producer with continuous production on Vilje.

fields.name: Visund
fields.statusText: The strategy for the Visund field is to maintain reservoir pressure within drilling limits and optimise oil recovery, while increasing gas exports. New production wells are being drilled continuously, some with exploration targets.

fields.name: Visund Sør
fields.statusText: The production started up again in September 2023 after a temporary shut-in due to low reservoir pressure and high water production. One new well was drilled in 2023 and is producing from the Statfjord reservoir. Start-up attempts have been made to get shut-in wells back to production.

fields.name: Volund
fields.statusText: The recoverable volume estimates are significantly higher than in the original PDO, but the field is on decline with a high water cut.

fields.name: Volve
fields.statusText: Volve was shut down in 2016, and the facility was removed in 2018.

fields.name: Yggdrasil
fields.statusText: Yggdrasil is the joint development of the Hugin, Munin, Fulla and Hugin Satellites fields, operated by Aker BP, with a shared processing platform and power from shore. Production is planned to start in 2027. Feltverdi shows the four Sodir fields as one asset; owner shares are weighted by each field's recoverable volumes.

fields.name: Yme
fields.statusText: Yme has had stable production since start-up in 2021 but has now entered the late phase. The focus going forward is to mitigate production decline through planned well interventions and reprocessing of seismic data to identify new infill targets.

fields.name: Yttergryta
fields.statusText: Yttergryta was shut down in 2012. The facility on Yttergryta is disconnected from the Midgard X template and will be decommissioned at the same time as the Åsgard facilities.

fields.name: Ærfugl Nord
fields.statusText: Water breakthrough in the well in 2023 has resulted in a significant reduction in the estimated recoverable reserves compared to the original PDO.

fields.name: Ørn
fields.statusText: The Production started in August 2026.

fields.name: Øst Frigg
fields.statusText: Øst Frigg was shut down in 1997, and the subsea templates were removed in 2001. The field is being redeveloped as part of Hugin in the Yggdrasil area.

fields.name: Åsgard
fields.statusText: Work is ongoing to increase the recovery from the field, with focus on a further reduction of inlet pressure on the facilities and identification of new targets for infill drilling. A development project for enabling lower inlet pressure on Åsgard B is ongoing. Subsea gas compression has accelerated and prolonged gas production at Åsgard. New tie-ins to Åsgard, such as Blåbjørn and Smørbukk Nord, contribute to prolonging the lifetime of the facilities.

fields.name: Aasta Hansteen
fields.statusText: The production went off plateau in 2024 and low pressure production has started. The Irpa field is under construction as a subsea tie-back to Aasta Hansteen.
